engine-b1-a1.reason: Tables pinned to the left wall, two pillars doing nothing, a huge empty middle. Reads like a lobby, not a cozy cafe.

fuzzy-b1-a2.reason: A busy, readable cafe floor: tables, counters, plants, and an obvious walk from the door to the counter.

full-b1-a2.reason: Nook walls overcomplicate a cozy cafe; a customer needs the floor plan explained to find the counter.

full-b2-a3.reason: Four shelves and one table is a pamphlet rack in an empty hall. This is not a library yet.

fuzzy-b2-a2.reason: The stacks work, but counters parked mid-floor do not belong in a library.

engine-b2-a2.reason: Dense shelf stacks with three reading tables; walks like a real library.

full-b3-a2.reason: A cover field of pillars and crates between two clean lanes. Reads as a dungeon entry hall.

full-b4-a3.reason: Counters scattered mid-floor read cafe, not flower shop; the buckets clump in one column.

engine-b4-a2.reason: Bucket rows read as display shelves, a counter right at the door, and a clean aisle to the bouquet counter.

fuzzy-b5-a1.reason: Stalls lined along one side, crates opposite, one wide lane to the food stall. Reads as a market street.

full-b5-a1.reason: Stall-and-crate stripes read as warehouse racking, not a night market.

engine-b5-a2.reason: Stalls ring the walls while crates squat in the middle; the market has no lane to walk.

full-b6-a3.reason: I count one dead end. The brief asked for at least two; this is a corridor with an alcove, not a maze.

full-b1-rev.reason: Fixed the complaint: open floor, clear route to the counter. It is the accepted cafe with the furniture rearranged, which is exactly what it was told to study.

full-b2-rev.reason: Went from pamphlet rack to full stacks; shelves line two walls now, tables by the nook.

engine-b5-rev.reason: Stalls and crates in a uniform checker grid. Still no row, no lane. More storage than market.
